'A tile's trend line that never changes is drawn flat along the bottom

'The spec now says a tile's trend line shows direction, not level: each tile scales its line between its own lowest and highest point, so a figure that never changes is a flat line along the bottom, whatever the figure is. No case checks this.

'Dashboard spec, Story 4, rule S4-R11b, added in version 45 on 14 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward, in answer to our question 1 of 14 Oct (his answer sheet, same day). The spec's change log, filled in later the same day (version 46), lists it under 2026-10-14. Page change: https://shopview.atlassian.net/wiki/pages/diffpagesbyversion.action?pageId=788430850&selectedPageVersions=44&selectedPageVersions=45

'Signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin).
A desktop browser window at least 1024 pixels wide, at 100% zoom.
A location where, this month, every technician's clocked time is on work orders only (no internal time) on at least two different days, so Technician Utilization is 100% on every day with clocked time (for example ZZAUTOTEST Flat Shop).
The same location has invoices this month on at least two days with different totals (for example $100.00 on one day and $400.00 on another).

'1. Click Dashboard in the top bar (all tiles on This Month).
2. Read the Technician Utilization headline.
3. Look at the Technician Utilization trend line.
4. Look at the Revenue trend line.

'Step 2: The headline reads 100.00%.
Step 3: The trend line is drawn as a flat line along the bottom of the trend area, not in the middle and not at the top. It is not the dashed empty-chart outline.
Step 4: The Revenue line uses the whole height of the trend area: its lowest day touches the bottom and its highest day touches the top.

'The value scale of the expanded charts (starting at 0) does not apply to the small trend line on a tile.
'A tile's date picker offers a custom range of up to 366 days and Today in the calendar

'The spec now says the tile uses the reports' date picker: the nine presets, plus a calendar for a custom range of up to 366 days with a Today button inside the calendar (not a tenth preset). A custom range is not remembered between visits. No case checks Today, the 366-day limit or that a custom range is forgotten.

'Dashboard spec, Story 7, rule S7-R2a, added in version 45 on 14 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward, in answer to our question 3 of 14 Oct (his answer sheet, same day). The spec's change log, filled in later the same day (version 46), lists it under 2026-10-14. Page change: https://shopview.atlassian.net/wiki/pages/diffpagesbyversion.action?pageId=788430850&selectedPageVersions=44&selectedPageVersions=45

'Signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin).
A desktop browser window at least 1024 pixels wide, at 100% zoom.
Any location with Reports data (for example the location you normally test in).

'1. Click Dashboard in the top bar.
2. Click the Revenue tile's date pill and read the list of presets.
3. Find the Today button and click it, then click Apply.
4. Read the Revenue pill and headline.
5. Open the Revenue pill again, pick a start day and an end day 366 days apart (the readout at the bottom reads "Range: 366 days") and click Apply.
6. Open the pill again and try to pick a range one day longer ("Range: 367 days").
7. Close the browser tab, open the site again in the same browser and click Dashboard.
8. Read the Revenue pill.

'Step 2: The presets are the nine named ones (Last 12 Months to Last Week). Today is not one of them.
Step 3: The Today button sits inside the calendar.
Step 4: The pill shows today's date only (for example "Oct 14, 2026 - Oct 14, 2026") and the headline equals the Sales report total for today.
Step 5: The 366-day range is accepted and the tile shows it.
Step 6: A range longer than 366 days cannot be applied.
Step 8: The pill reads This Month again: the custom range was not remembered.

'At Risk table: a customer's revenue link opens a Sales report with the same total

'The spec now says a customer's twelve-month revenue in the At Risk Customers table is a link to the Sales report for that customer over the same twelve months, so the report total equals the amount, and that a walk-in row or a $0.00 amount is plain text. C540783 checks the link and the customer filter, but not the total or the plain-text rows.

'Dashboard spec, Story 6, rule S6-R8a, added in version 45 on 14 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward, in answer to our question 4 of 14 Oct (his answer sheet, same day). The spec's change log, filled in later the same day (version 46), lists it under 2026-10-14. Page change: https://shopview.atlassian.net/wiki/pages/diffpagesbyversion.action?pageId=788430850&selectedPageVersions=44&selectedPageVersions=45

'1. Click Dashboard in the top bar and click View details on At Risk Customers.
2. Write down {Customer-A}'s Revenue (12 Mo).
3. Click {Customer-A}'s Revenue (12 Mo) amount.
4. Read the Sales report's customer filter, its dates and its Totals row Subtotal.
5. Go back to the Dashboard and open the At Risk Customers details again.
6. Point at and click {Customer-B}'s $0.00 amount.
7. Point at and click the walk-in row's amount, if there is one.

'Step 4: The Sales report is filtered to {Customer-A} only, over the twelve months the amount covers (from the 1st of the month eleven months back to today), and its Totals row Subtotal equals the amount from step 2, to the cent.
Step 6: The $0.00 amount is plain text: the pointer does not change to a hand and clicking does nothing.
Step 7: The walk-in amount is plain text in the same way. If your location has no walk-in row, write 'walk-in row not reachable by hand' in the result comment.

'Which twelve months the amount covers is taken from the spec's "Last 12 months" window, which every report the dashboard links to uses.
'The expanded Revenue chart follows the Revenue tile's date range

'The spec now says the expanded Revenue chart covers the tile's own date range, with one bar per day, week, month or quarter by the same rule as the trend line: This Month shows daily bars, Last 12 Months twelve monthly bars. No case checks a range other than Last 12 Months.

'Dashboard spec, Story 6, rule S6-R3a, added in version 45 on 14 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward, in answer to our question 5 of 14 Oct (his answer sheet, same day). The spec's change log, filled in later the same day (version 46), lists it under 2026-10-14. Page change: https://shopview.atlassian.net/wiki/pages/diffpagesbyversion.action?pageId=788430850&selectedPageVersions=44&selectedPageVersions=45

'Signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin).
A desktop browser window at least 1024 pixels wide, at 100% zoom.
A location with invoices on several days this month, last quarter and over the last twelve months.

'1. Click Dashboard in the top bar (Revenue on This Month) and click View details on Revenue.
2. Read the labels along the bottom of the Revenue chart and count the bars.
3. Set the Revenue pill to Last Quarter.
4. Read the chart's labels and count the bars.
5. Set the Revenue pill to Last 12 Months.
6. Read the chart's labels and count the bars.

'Step 2: One bar per day of this month, labelled by day, not by month.
Step 4: One bar per week (about 13 bars) for the three months of last quarter.
Step 6: Twelve bars, one per month, from the 1st of the month eleven months back to this month (for example Nov 2025 to Oct 2026).
Steps 2, 4 and 6: The bars always add up to the Revenue headline for the same range.
